NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE-1 ZONING MAP AMENDMENT AT
920-928 WEST DIVERSEY PARKWAY

The Applicant requests a zoning change for the property located at 920-928 West Diversey Parkway (the
“Property”) from the B3-2 Community Shopping District to B2-5 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District to
construct a 5-story, 65.0 foot, mixed-use building with 52 residential units, 3,400 square feet of
commercial square footage and a floor area ratio of 3.9 (48,695 s.f.). The proposed development will
have 8 parking spaces, 52 bicycle parking spaces and one loading space. The subject property is located
in a transit served location.

The Project is approximately 140 feet from the Diversey CTA train stop. Accordingly, only 26 parking
spaces are required (50 percent of the number of residential units).

Lot Area 12,400 sq. ft.
Floor Area Ratio 3.90
Building Area (for FAR calculation only) 48,695 sq. ft.
Density (Lot Area per Dwelling Unit) 238.46 sq. ft. per unit
Number of Dwelling Units $2
Off-Street Parking 8 spaces
Bicycle Parking 52 spaces
Setbacks:
Front Q’-0”
Side (north) 0’-0”
Side (south) 0-0”
Rear 87-8” 2)
Building Height 65’-0”

The Project requires the following zoning relief in accordance with the review and approval procedures
set forth in Section 17-13-0303-D of the Zoning Ordinance, which were approved as part of the Original
Zoning Application:

‘An administrative adjustment for the reduction of the required parking count from twenty-six
(26) parking spaces to eight (8) parking spaces (Section 17-13-1003-EE); and

® A variation to reduce the rear setback from the required combined 30.0 feet to 8.0 feet, 8.0
inches (Section 17-13-1101-B); and

&) All relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for the attached Plans.

[continued on next page]

Section 17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations.

(1) The Project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B of the Zoning
Ordinance such that the Project (i) is located within 1,320 feet from a CTA bus line corridor and
2,640 feet from a CTA rail station, (ii) is located in a B zoning district, and (iii) proposes at least
1:1 bicycle parking. The project will not have parking spaces in excess of 50% of the Minimum
Automobile Parking Ratio for the subject zoning district.

(2) The Project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504 of the Zoning
Ordinance as follows:

(i) _ the Project is subject to Section 17-3-0308 and therefore is subject to Section 17-3-
0504 (§17-3-0504-A);

Gi) the building is located within 5.0 feet of the sidewalk on West Diversey Parkway, its
only street frontage (§17-3-0504-B);

(iii) the building complies with transparency standards appliable to buildings on
pedestrian streets (§17-3-0504-C);

(iv) _ the primary entrance to the Project is on West Diversey Parkway. The Project does
not abut a pedestrian street (§17-3-0504-D);

(v) _ the Project is not a nonresidential use such that Paragraph E is not applicable (§17-3-
0504-E);

(vi) all off-street vehicle parking at the Project is located in the rear of the building (§17-
3-0504-F);

(vii) vehicle access to the rear parking area is from the alley north of Diversey Street (from
Sheffield Avenue) (§17-3-0504-G);

(viii) the Project is not located along a pedestrian street such that Paragraph H is not
applicable (§17-3-0504-H);

(ix) the Project is a residential use such that Paragraph I is not applicable ($17-3-0504-]);
and

(x) the encouraged uses set forth in Paragraph J are noted. The proposed use of the
ground floor commercial space is to be determined (§17-3-0504-J).

(3) The Project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly Development Guide:
Station Area Typology for a “Major Activity Center”, which encourages higher density
residential uses near such rail stations with integrated retail.

(4) — The Project will not have a number of parking space in excess of 50% of the Minimum
Automobile Parking Ratio for the B zoning district.

(5) The Project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules of the Chicago
Department of Transportation (“CDOT”), and will be reviewed by CDOT in accordance with
that Plan.
